title: Select first float-state batch
strategy: Architect v2 Wave C. Sol ranked the five retained float-state targets and diagnosed V1; Luna compiled two bounded hypotheses in the original unit and stopped at Sol's discriminator.

ranking.evidence: One confirmed direct caller at 0x80006B10 supplies a Gfx cursor in $a0 and f32 step bits in $a1; small typed leaf with recoverable command writes and loop behavior.
Clears twelve timing slots and ten float globals; no direct incoming reference found.
Four direct calls from 0x8000693C reveal a cursor, color, float operands and row argument; several command paths and FPU rounding increase risk.
Initializes display-list state and calls 0x80006BF8 four times and 0x80006B44 once; no direct incoming reference found.
Fourteen-entry timing dispatcher with 64-bit conversions; no direct incoming reference found.

arguments.$a1: f32 step bits, moved from $f20 after signed divide-to-f32

observed_behavior: Advance the display-list cursor and emit the E700 pair in w1-then-w0 store order, then emit the F700 pair in w0-then-w1 order.
Read signed global D_8005B230_5BE30; a negative value returns after the two initial command pairs.
For a nonnegative bound, truncate the f32 step once and emit inclusive indexed F6 pairs using the low ten coordinate bits.
Reload D_8005B230_5BE30 at the loop tail; preserve cursor advancement and the original per-command word order.
abi_and_behavior.uncertainty: Caller and ROM instruction evidence close the input ABI and command path. The host buffer tests validate semantics but do not prove native store order or global reloads.

model_review.sol_6_1_high_ranking: Selected 0x80006B44 as the only native candidate: shortest target with one caller that closes the cursor and f32 argument types. Larger functions had unresolved incoming-call evidence or materially more FPU/dispatch complexity.
model_review.v1_diagnosis: REGISTER_LIFETIME and scheduling mismatch, not ABI or relocation. Original keeps packet pointer in $v1, truncated step in $a1 and loop index in $a2; V1 uses $v0, $v1 and $a1. Differences span prologue, guard/conversion, body and loop tail.
model_review.v2_approval: Initialize i=0 before the signed gate and use that same induction value in the guard, preserving do/while, volatile reads, conversion placement, command stores and loop body. Predicted move $a2,$zero before bltz, mfc1 $a1 after trunc.w.s, multu $a1,$a2 and a tail compare using $a2.
model_review.v2_result: Mismatch count improved from 38 to 36 words, but first mismatch remained lw $v1,0($a0) versus lw $v0,0($a0). The predicted move became move $v1,$zero; mfc1 $a1 was at +0x60 rather than +0x5C, and multiply/tail comparison used $v1 rather than $a2.
model_review.stop_rule: Freeze after this Sol-approved V2. No unrelated syntax or qualifier variants.

variant_budget.historical_needs_context_excluded: An older needs_context/untyped_structure row had no source variant or measured native mismatch and was not replayed or counted.
variant_budget.stop_reason: Sol's V2 discriminator failed: first saved-register mismatch persisted and predicted loop-register roles did not appear.

native_candidates.hypothesis: Emit observed command words through Gfx fields, use a signed volatile global gate, truncate the float once, and loop while reloading the gate after each F6 pair.
Sol-approved: initialize i before the signed gate and use the same value in the guard, retaining the original conversion, volatile reads, stores and do/while loop.
